Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

answer verb and noun

also reply, respond, an answer, response, answer point by point, answer your questions, that’s not an answer to my question

classical

Plin. Ep. 4.13.3: respondit: «etiam.»
Traupman 28, 33: respondē mihi

1respondeō, respōnsum: short e in re- (Lewis & Short rē-spondeo, rēsponsum). The prefix is re-, from Proto-Italic *wre, “back” (de Vaan 516, s.v. re-, red-). Lewis & Short writes rē- before sc, sp and st, and only there. Its article on the prefix gives rĕ, with a by-form rĕd-, and puts the poets’ rēdūcō, rēlātum down to “the suppression of the d”; the long mark before s and a consonant seems to rest on the same idea, as its dī-scindō from dis- does. Bennett (The Latin Language §48) rejects that lengthening for ascendō, distinguō, suspiciō as “an untenable theory of compensatory lengthening”, and Lewis’s own Elementary Latin Dictionary (1890) prints re-spondeō. Traupman writes respondēre too. Ruling: re- short before sc, sp, st.

respondeō1, respondēre, respondī, respōnsum

verb, second conjugation

answer, reply

With a dative of the person (respondē mihi) and an accusative, or ad and the accusative, for what is answered (ad ea, quae quaesīta erant, respondēbat, Cic. Phil. 1.2). To answer a letter is rescrībere.

Other words

  • respōnsum1, respōnsī n. — an answer, a reply

    noun, second declension · classical · Quint. 1.5.36: cum respōnsum ab interrogante dissentit; Traupman 28: alicui respōnsum reddō

    Respōnsum reddere or dare, to give an answer.

Examples

  • huic ego «studēs?» inquam. respondit: «etiam.» «ubi?» «Mediōlānī.» «cūr nōn hīc?»

    I asked him, “Do you go to school?” He answered, “Yes.” “Where?” “In Milan.” “Why not here?”Plin. Ep. 4.13.3

  • aliud mihi respondēs ac rogō?

    You answer something other than what I ask?Ter. Ph. 684

  • interrogantibus libenter respondeat, nōn interrogantēs percontētur ultrō

    let him gladly answer those who ask, and question those who do notQuint. 2.2.6

  • Tibi respondēbō ad singula.

    I’ll answer you point by point.Traupman 93

  • Nunc respondēbō ad ea quae rogāvistī.

    Now I’ll answer your questions.Traupman 93

See also ask, say, hear.
